description: Blacklist regex patterns for @-command paths that should be treated as plain text (derived from log @ symbol analysis). All regexes are applied to the path part after '@'. Each pattern includes a short description explaining typical examples and why it should NOT be resolved as a workspace file.

patterns.name: timestamp_file_or_id
patterns.description: Android/Systemd-style timestamp IDs or timestamp-based log filenames such as 1765789849649, 1765789849649.txt or 1765789849649.txt.gz. These usually come from logs and are not repo file paths.

patterns.name: systemd_service_unit
patterns.description: Systemd service unit names like configfs.service or systemd-journald.service. These are unit identifiers, not files in the current project.

patterns.name: unix_domain_socket
patterns.description: Unix domain socket paths under /dev/socket/ (for example /dev/socket/logdw). These refer to runtime sockets on the host system, not source files.

patterns.name: audio_bus_tag
patterns.description: Audio bus or media tags such as :BUS00_MEDIA or :BUS01_SPKR. These are logical bus identifiers, not file system paths.

patterns.name: resolution_tag
patterns.description: Resolution markers like 600w_800h_1c that encode width/height/channels (e.g. image or video formats). They are metadata strings, not filenames.

patterns.name: irq_or_controller_id
patterns.description: IRQ/controller-style IDs such as b220000-9 or 1a2b-3, commonly seen in low-level logs. These represent hardware identifiers, not project file paths.
